Why do soda bubbles rise from the same spots?
Why do soda bubbles rise from the same spots?
Each string usually
starts at a tiny speck
of lint stuck
to the glass.
Soda is packed
with carbon dioxide,
forced in under pressure.
Open it,
and the gas wants out,
but starting a bubble is hard.
A brand-new bubble
is so tiny that surface
tension squeezes its gas
back into the drink.
It needs a head start:
a pocket of gas that's
already there.
Hollow fibres,
like towel lint,
trap exactly that.
Each one fills with gas
and lets go of a bubble,
again and again.
The gas comes
from the drink.
The starting points are
bits of lint
on the glass.
